newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's BBV cuts prime rate, eyeing inflation.
newsitem.headline: Spain's BBV cuts prime rate, eyeing inflation.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) said on Tuesday it cut its prime lending rate to 8.0 percent versus 8.25 percent effective from today.
In a statement the bank said that the new cut is due to favourable expectations for April inflation.
"Our economic research department forecasts that inflation will break two percent in April and could be around 1.5 percent in May," BBV said. April CPI is due on May 14.
BBV previously cut rates on January 16.
Since then the Bank of Spain cut its key rate twice for a total reduction of 50 basis points.
